raw_response:
Looking at my situation — 58 years old, land in Quzhou, middle school education — I know what works here and what doesn't. My father grew wheat and maize on this same ground. I grew wheat and maize. That's what this county does, that's what the grain station buys, and I'm not about to change things at my age and risk everything on something new.

My land is about 15 mu total. I'll put 13 mu into the wheat-maize rotation like always — winter wheat goes in October, harvest in June, then I plant summer maize right after on the same ground, harvest in September. This double-cropping is what makes sense here. I'll keep 2 mu near the house for vegetables — garlic, cabbage, whatever the family needs, maybe sell some at the county market.

For wheat, I'll buy the improved variety from the agri-input shop in town — probably Jimai or something the shop owner says is popular this year. I don't trust my own saved seed anymore since yields dropped a few years back. I'll apply base fertilizer before sowing — compound fertilizer plus some urea, same as last year. I'll irrigate four times: the winter water in November, then return-green, jointing, and grain-filling water. Groundwater well still works fine. I'll spray twice — once for powdery mildew in spring, once for aphids before heading.

For maize, I'll plant hybrid seed — Zhengdan 958 is what most people in my village use. After wheat harvest I'll plant directly without ploughing, just rotary till the stubble in. Less work. Water once or twice if it doesn't rain. One pesticide spray for corn borer.

At 58 my back isn't what it was, so I try to use the village machinery cooperative for harvesting. I'll do the hand work myself to save money.
